newsitem.title: UK: Ulster Unionists in Euro-pact with Goldsmith.
newsitem.headline: Ulster Unionists in Euro-pact with Goldsmith.

text.p: The Ulster Unionist Party (UUP) said on Monday an alliance it was forging in the European parliament with Anglo-French financier Sir James Goldsmith would not affect how it votes in the British parliament.

Now that he has lost his majority in the lower House of Commons, Prime Minister John Major depends for survival on the support of the nine Ulster Unionists members of parliament, who represent Northern Ireland's pro-British Protestant majority.

"This is a change being made in the European Parliament. It has no implications for parliament at Westminster. It does not involve any change of policy as far as Westminster is concerned," UUP leader David Trimble told a news conference.
The alliance is a warning to Major that the Ulster Unionists' votes cannot be taken for granted in the run-up to Britian's general election, which must be held by May 22.

But Trimble said there was no formal link between his party and Goldsmith, who leads the Autre France party in the Strasbourg parliament and has founded the Referendum party to fight the British election.

"We will continue to vote in the same way as we do and have done in the House of Commons. We are not going to behave in a capricious or irresponsible manner in terms of voting over the course of the next few months.
"We will consider each matter very carefully in terms of its implications and we will be voting as Ulster Unionists," he said.
Under the pact, the sole UU member of the European parliament in Strasbourg, Jim Nicholson, will quit the pro-EU European People's Party grouping to join Goldsmith's Europe of Nations faction.
In return, the Referendum party will support the Ulster Unionists' campaign in Northern Ireland on the specific issue of a plebisicite on Britain's role in the European Union.
Goldsmith created the Referendum party with the sole purpose of forcing a referendum and he plans to field hundreds of candidates at the election.
Trimble said reports that Goldmsith intended to funnel part of his 20 million pound ($33 million) election war chest to the Ulster Unionists were "inappropriate".

"The Referendum party says it is going allocate some of its promotional budget for the purpose of supporting a referendum in terms of addressing that to the people of Northern Ireland... We do not expect any money to come to the Ulster Unionist Party under that heading," he said.
Trimble said his party was not anti-European but did oppose the drive to turn the EU into an integrated nation state.
The alliance has split the UUP, Northern Ireland's largest political party.
Deputy leader John Taylor said the party's policy committee had been shocked to learn of the alliance.
He stressed it would not give Goldsmith influence over the way the UU votes in the Westminster parliament.
"What worries me of course is that they're here and they may be away tomorrow. Where would we be then?" he said on Sky TV. ($1=.6002 Pound)
